new_authors_found: Skinner, James Scott — Scottish fiddle: 'A Guide to Bowing, Strathspey and Reel Playing' (Paterson, 1900) is the classic bowing book; not on IMSLP and not verified here
Cohen, Jeremy — jazz violin: 'Stylistic Etudes for Solo Violin' (Violin Jazz Publishing), listed intermediate/advanced on a US university list; not verified
Snidero, Jim — Advance Music 'Easy Jazz Conception' violin edition (15 solo études for jazz phrasing); said to be easy, unverified
Arias-Gago Marino, Antonio — Spain: nine-cuaderno 'Antología de estudios para violín' (Real Musical 1975-86), a conservatory standard; per-volume contents needed
Gola, Zdeněk — Czech: Vibrato method (Japanese edition, Ongaku no Tomo Sha 2017) and school books; for the Czech researcher
Bron, Zakhar — Russian: 'Etüdenkunst' étude collection (Ries & Erler 1999, with Daishin Kashimoto); for the Russian researcher

note: Method: IMSLP nationality categories (about 50 nationalities, intersected with the IMSLP Methods/Studies/Exercises/Scales/Caprices dumps), IMSLP page fields and publisher data, then national catalogues (Nasjonalbiblioteket, LIBRIS, NDL Search, Open Library) and publisher listings (Carl Fischer via Performers Music, Yamaha Sheet Music, Hal Leonard). All 10 searches were used. Confidence: most entries are existence-verified but level-unverified (levels are guesses from genre or contents lists); the Lange items (Op. 6 Hefte 1-4, Tekniske Studier, Praktisk violinskole Del 3) rest on NB catalogue records only because the copies are restricted. Bang: Carl Fischer listings (Performers Music) give Part III = third and second positions, IV = fourth and fifth, V = sixth and seventh, VI = bowing/staccato; Part I/II below floor; Part VII exists per the Dover note ('Part I of seven parts') but no contents list was found. IMSLP holds Parts I-V only. Suzuki Violin School Vols 4-10 treated as repertoire (skipped), consistent with exam_boards; Position Etudes is in exam_boards. Duplicates left to other groups: Alonso (italian_baroque), Praeger (concert_etudes), Monasterio/Libon (franco_b and italian_baroque: their levels differ, Monasterio Vol. 1 is L5 in franco_b and L4 in italian_baroque), Quiroga (italian_baroque), Lvov (russian_soviet). Checked and fine: catalogue id 666 (José White, 6 Études Op. 13, solo violin, Schonenberger Paris 1869, dedicated to Alard, Sivori, Vieuxtemps, Wieniawski, Léonard, Arango); franco_b's Op. 33 'Nouvelles études' is a separate set of 6 études (Durdilly, Paris c. 1902, dedicated to Joachim). Not found or not verifiable: technical books by Manén, Arbós, Brosa, Díaz Albertini (no IMSLP works or Wikipedia mention); Chinese, Korean, Indian, Latin American (apart from White), Baltic, Armenian, Georgian, Romanian, Greek, Israeli, Canadian/Australian/NZ/South African violin technique books (searches and catalogues gave nothing verifiable; Finnish Finna API returned 403, Danish catalogues not reachable, IMSLP scans are behind a bot check so no scan was inspected). Japanese: the only verified Japanese-authored technical book is Ono's scale method (Russian-born author); other Japanese titles are listed in skipped.
